article_sentences: Mumbai terror attack survivor Moshe Holtzberg is studying to become a rabbi in New York, while Nariman House is being renovated to house Chabad activities, a museum and a memorial, Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky said.

Mumbai: Moshe Holtzberg, the Israeli boy popularly known as ‘Baby Moshe’, who survived the 2008 Nariman House terror attack in which his parents were killed, is pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and aspires to become a rabbi like his father.

Rabbi Israel Kozlovsky, who is in charge of Nariman House, one of the places targeted by Pakistani Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists during the November 26, 2008 attacks, said he met Moshe two weeks ago at a rabbinical conference in New York.

“The conference was attended by 4,000 to 5,000 rabbis from across the world, and Moshe was also present,” Kozlovsky said, showing a photograph on his mobile phone of Moshe posing in traditional attire alongside other rabbis.
A rabbi is a spiritual leader, religious teacher and legal scholar.
In the photograph, the once two-year-old ‘Baby Moshe’, whose footage of sobbing inconsolably after the attack drew global attention and moved millions, appears as a 20-year-old man.
“He is currently pursuing rabbinical studies in New York and wants to become a rabbi.
Hopefully, he will return to India.
That is our hope,” Kozlovsky told PTI on Wednesday.
Moshe’s parents, Rabbi Gavriel Holtzberg and Rivka Holtzberg, were killed when terrorists stormed the Chabad House, a centre that served the Jewish community here.
Moshe’s nanny, Sandra Samuel, rescued him from the building and fled.
He later moved to Israel to stay with his grandparents.

stories.headline: Nepal floods: Indian Embassy seeks verification of missing Indians by 2 Dec
stories.title: Nepal floods: Indian Embassy seeks verification of missing Indians by 2 Dec
stories.summary: Nepal floods: Indian Embassy seeks verification of missing Indians by 2 Dec
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Embassy of India in Nepal has urged families of Indian nationals missing since the devastating floods of August 26 to check their details against a list released by Nepali authorities and submit any objections or corrections by 2 December 2026.

Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) has published the names of 213 missing Indian nationals as part of a process to presume their deaths and formally declare them dead.
The disasters have claimed more than 1,400 lives, while over 5,000 people, including foreign nationals, remain missing.
The Nepali government has decided to initiate the formal declaration of death for those still unaccounted for after completing the required legal procedures.
The floods also caused extensive damage to infrastructure along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, affecting around a dozen hydropower projects.
In a statement, the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu asked relatives to verify the published details and submit their concerns or proposed amendments by 2 December.
"After completing the process of seeking comments/amendments, the Government of Nepal will finalise the list and formally issue the declaration of death," the embassy said.
Once the list is finalised, the embassy will facilitate the process of obtaining death certificates for the individuals from the concerned local authorities in Nepal, it added.
The embassy said families might be asked to provide additional information and documents during the process.
It also assured them that further updates would be shared in the coming days.
According to an NDRRMA notice, the authority has received verified details of 452 missing foreign nationals through diplomatic missions of 12 countries.

Of these, 213 are Indian nationals, 85 Chinese, 69 Americans, 32 British, 27 Canadians, nine Singaporeans, six South Africans, four French nationals, two each from Hungary, Belgium and Kazakhstan, and one from Belarus.

stories.headline: Inter-ministerial central team reviews damage caused by heavy rains, floods in Jammu
stories.title: Inter-ministerial central team reviews damage caused by heavy rains, floods in Jammu
stories.summary: Jammu, Nov 25: An Inter-Ministerial Central Team, led by Union Joint Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, Gaya Parsad, today reviewed the extent of damages caused by heavy rains, flash floods, cloudbursts and landslides across Jammu Division. The meeting was chaired by Joint Secretary Gaya Parsad along with Commissioner Secretary, Department of Disaster Management, Relief, Rehabilitation and Reconstruction, M. Raju and Divisional Commissioner Jammu, Vikas Kundal, at the Conference Hall of the Divisional Commissioner’s Office. The Government of India has deputed the Inter-Ministerial Central Team to undertake an on-the-spot assessment of the damages caused by the natural calamities. The team comprises officials from the Ministries of Road Transport and Highways, Power, Rural Development, Jal Shakti and Finance, and will visit the affected areas to assess the ground situation. The meeting was attended by Chief Engineer, JPDCL; Director General, School Education, Jammu; Director, Rural Development; Director, Agriculture; Director, Animal Husbandry; Chief Engineer, PWD (R&B), Jammu, and other concerned officers. Deputy Commissioners of all districts of Jammu Division participated in the meeting virtually. During the meeting, a detailed PowerPoint presentation was made, highlighting the extent of damage to public infrastructure and private property, besides the loss of human lives caused by the recent natural calamities. The Divisional Commissioner apprised the Central Team of the affected areas and the magnitude of damages to critical infrastructure, including roads, power infrastructure and water supply schemes. He also briefed the team about the restoration measures undertaken by various departments to ensure the early restoration of essential services. A detailed deliberation was held on the challenges arising from incessant rains, flash floods and landslides, which had disrupted normal life across the region. Officers from various departments shared sector-wise details of the damages and apprised the team of the measures initiated for restoration and rehabilitation. Joint Secretary Gaya Parsad emphasised the need for accurate and comprehensive damage assessment based on ground-level verification. He directed the concerned departments to prepare sector-wise damage reports, submit realistic estimates in accordance with the prescribed norms and furnish complete supporting documentation. He further stressed the importance of accounting for expenditure already incurred and ensuring that there was no duplication while preparing damage estimates and proposals. Over the next few days, the Inter-Ministerial Central Team will undertake detailed field visits to various affected areas across Jammu Division to assess the actual extent of losses and damages.

stories.headline: Karnataka HC quashes FIR over alleged tampering in 2023 Sringeri election
stories.title: Karnataka HC quashes FIR over alleged tampering in 2023 Sringeri election
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Karnataka High Court has quashed criminal proceedings against former BJP MLA DN Jeevaraj and two election officials over alleged tampering with postal ballots in the 2023 Sringeri Assembly election.
The court held that the complaint, filed nearly three years after the original counting, was too delayed to sustain the prosecution.
In an order passed on November 21, Justice M Nagaprasanna set aside the FIR registered by Chikkamagaluru Town.
Police against Jeevaraj, former Deputy Commissioner KN Ramesh and Returning Officer TR Vedamurthy.
The case involved allegations of forgery, criminal conspiracy and violations of the Representation of the People Act (1951).
The complaint was filed on May 3, 2026, by Sudhir Kumar Murolli, an election agent and authorised representative of Congress candidate TD Rajegowda.
It alleged that postal ballots had been tampered with after the original counting on May 13, 2023, including ballots that had been cast in Rajegowda's favour.
The complaint also alleged that ballot box seals had been removed and ballot paper account sheets altered to secure an electoral advantage.
The complaint came hours after a recount ordered by the High Court resulted in Jeevaraj being declared the winner of the Sringeri constituency.
The original result had gone in Rajegowda's favour by a margin of 201 votes, with 279 postal ballots rejected.
Jeevaraj had challenged the election result through an election petition.
On April 6, 2026, the High Court partly allowed his petition and directed the Returning Officer to re-verify the 279 rejected postal ballots and recount all postal ballots.

stories.headline: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
stories.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
stories.summary: Seoul, Nov 26: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons, days after ignoring US President Donald Trump's offer to meet during his recent visit to Asia. Kim's statement signals again that he won't give up his evolving nuclear program — the backbone of his authoritarian rule — and is eager to bolster his country's status as a nuclear power. The North's official Korean Central News Agency said Thursday that Kim inspected two nuclear materials production factories, one newly inaugurated and the other being expanded. KCNA photos showed Kim and senior military officials walking between dense rows of what appeared to be centrifuges used to produce weapons-grade uranium and touring halls displaying what were believed to be warheads. Some of the images were blurred. KCNA said Kim visited a nuclear-powered equipment production base and a nuclear research institute as well on Wednesday. North Korea has disclosed a uranium enrichment site a few times since it showed one at its main Yongbyon nuclear complex to visiting American scholars in 2010. North Korea didn't say where the nuclear materials production factories that Kim visited this week are located. In June, when North Korea disclosed parts of a uranium enrichment site while reporting on Kim's visit there, outside experts assessed it was likely an additional uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon. Kim justifies nuke program by citing threats from US, South Korea Kim said his latest inspection visit was part of efforts to strengthen North Korea's defence capabilities in response to “variable nuclear threats approaching the Korean Peninsula moment by moment," KCNA said. He accused the US of inciting its regional allies to possess nuclear-powered submarines and committing to sharing its nuclear weapons with them, KCNA said. “The validity and substantiality of our possession of nuclear weapons and the trend of bolstering up its nuclear capability in quality and quantity are an irreversible reality,” Kim said, according to KCNA. Kim also said the deployment of low-yield battlefield nuclear weapons across multiple domains for various missions is crucial and urgent given North Korea's “inevitable reality facing the border with the most dangerous enemy state," a reference to South Korea. North Korea has in recent years focused on developing and deploying such tactical nuclear weapons amid heightened animosity with South Korea. South Korea's Defence Ministry said it takes Kim's comments on battlefield nuclear weapons seriously and added that Seoul maintains a firm military readiness against Pyongyang's nuclear threats under an alliance with the US. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff declined to share an analysis of the North Korean nuclear facilities reported by KCNA, calling it confidential information for South Korea and the US. Kim has accelerated the expansion of his military nuclear program since his earlier high-stakes diplomacy with Trump collapsed in 2019. He has also shifted his foreign policy focus toward strengthening ties with Cold War-era allies Moscow and Beijing, seeking to strengthen his regional footing while pushing to establish North Korea as a permanent nuclear power. Trump still hopes to meet Kim Trump reiterated his eagerness to restore diplomacy with Kim as he visited China last week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. But a Trump-Kim meeting didn't happen, with Pyongyang not publicly responding to Trump's overture. In an interview with the New York Post this week, Trump dismissed the suggestion that Kim had rebuffed his outreach, saying, “No, he didn't ignore it. You know, we had many leaders there … There'll be a time when we meet … It was just not really the right time. It was a very busy two-day period.” Trump also claimed he could revive diplomacy with Kim at any time by restarting the exchange of letters they maintained during his first term, although he acknowledged that the two leaders had not corresponded “recently.” Kim has previously said he could return to talks if the US drops its “hostile policy” against his country and respects what he calls the North's status as a nuclear state. Experts say Kim aims to win international recognition as a nuclear state so that he could demand the lifting of international sanctions. Last week, International Atomic Energy Agency Director General Rafael Grossi assessed North Korea has been expanding its original uranium enrichment facility at Yongbyon, calling the move “a cause for serious concern.” Nuclear weapons can be built using either highly enriched uranium or weapons-grade plutonium, and North Korea has facilities to produce both at Yongbyon. Last year, South Korea's Unification Minister Chung Dong-young said that North Korea was operating four uranium enrichment facilities and that they were running every day.

article_sentences: India-US trade deal: The latest US tariff rates announced on Wednesday indicate that Washington is willing to give India a competitive advantage over rival exporters, provided India agrees to finalise the long-pending trade agreement.
The Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed a 17% tariff on Indian exports if New Delhi “were to reach an agreement on Reciprocal Trade” with Washington.
However, in the absence of a trade agreement, India could face tariffs of up to 25% under Section 301 investigations covering excess production capacity that affects US interests.
In comparison, the USTR has proposed tariffs of 18% on Bangladesh, Cambodia and Thailand, and 20% on China and Vietnam, subject to the respective countries reaching trade agreements with the US.
This could give Indian exporters a competitive edge over their counterparts in these competing economies.
Earlier, in February, US President Donald Trump had announced a trade deal with India, claiming that New Delhi had agreed to significantly increase its purchases of American goods.
The announcement came after Washington agreed to reduce tariffs on Indian exports to 18% from the earlier rate of 50%.
According to V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited, the tariff threat is unlikely to have any impact on the Indian stock market in the near-term.
“The US administration has proposed 25% tariffs on India ( 17% if a trade deal is struck) along with tariffs proposed on many other countries.
This is more a tactic to apply pressure on India to reach a deal.
India is unlikely to relent much,” Vijayakumar said.

Furthermore, Shrikant Chouhan, Head of Equity Research at Kotak Neo, said that proposed US tariffs on Indian goods have largely been factored in by equity markets and are unlikely to disrupt the broader market rally.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (November 26, 2026) informed that an application to shift the Karthigai Deepam flame burning at the Deepa Mandapam to the Deepathoon located atop the Thirupparankundram Hill and contempt petitions filed against Tamil Nadu authorities for failing to comply with a November 20 order to light the sacred lamp on the stone pillar will be listed on November 27.
Justice Aravind Kumar, who headed the Bench, remarked about the proposed listing to lawyers who were representing the contempt petitioners during the oral mentioning hour.

In one of the contempt petitions, Hindu Dharma Parishad has sought the initiation of contempt action against T.G. Vinay, Commissioner, Hindu Religious & Charitable Endowments Department; Nishant Krishna, District Collector, Madurai; and Mr.S. Rajendiran, Madurai Commissioner of Police.

Mr. Krishna’s preliminary report, filed in the Supreme Court on November 25, stated that the district authorities had made all arrangements to facilitate the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepathoon in compliance with the November 20 order.
However, the Board of Trustees at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy Temple had not authorised persons for the lamp-lighting team on November 24.
“It amounts to invasion of legitimate expectation duly sanctioned by the Supreme Court,” the petition said.

The petition said the contemnors “deliberately failed and neglected to obey the orders of the Supreme Court” and violating the November 20 order, failing to adhere to their undertaking made in the Supreme Court and, thirdly, by making a false submission of complying with the directions passed by the apex court.
“The conduct of the alleged contemnors tantamount to gross contempt of the orders of this court and merits no sympathy.

As such, the Contemnors are liable to be awarded the strictest punishment under the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971… They have committed wilful breach and disobedience… The action of the accused tends to obstruct the administration of justice,” the petition said.

A similar contempt petition filed by an advocate, V. Ramasubbu, represented by K.V. Muthukumar, pointed out that the court’s direction to keep out unauthorised persons from the lamp-lighting ceremony was taken advantage of by the State authorities to issue a John Doe injunction on the general public.

The Hindu parties’ separate application, orally mentioned by senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar, is seeking directions to the State and temple authorities “to light the lamp at the Deepathoon either by igniting from and out of the same Deepam which is still burning at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple or make necessary arrangements in terms of order dated November 20, 2026”.
The application said the four Sthanikars had denied giving any opinion to light the lamp at the Deepa Mandapam nor were they consulted.

article_sentences: Guwahati: The Supreme Court of India on Thursday, November 26, 2026, directed the Union Government and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to introduce separate red hexagonal warning labels on packaged foods high in fat, sugar and salt.
The ruling, delivered in New Delhi, aims to strengthen consumer awareness and protect public health through clearer front-of-pack nutrition labelling.
A Division Bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice K Vinod Chandran rejected the approach of using one combined warning symbol for multiple nutrients of concern.
The court directed FSSAI to ensure that every nutrient receives its own clearly identifiable warning.
The judgment states, "The authority shall ensure that the FOPNL provides for a separate hexagon for each nutrient of concern...
rather than a single combined hexagon."
Under the direction, the front of packaged food products must display individual red hexagonal labels identifying HIGH FAT, HIGH SUGAR and HIGH SALT, depending on their nutritional composition.
The ruling replaces the regulator's August 2026 proposal, which had suggested a combined warning label.
The Supreme Court's decision followed a public interest litigation filed by 3S and Our Health Society, represented by advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi.
The petitioner sought stronger front-of-pack nutrition labelling to help consumers identify packaged foods containing high levels of fat, sugar and salt.
The court also addressed the nutritional thresholds proposed under Table 15.1 of the Dietary Guidelines for Indians (DGI) 2024.
The Bench said these nutritional values should not be adopted without modification because they account for added sugars and fats rather than total sugars and fats.

article_sentences: Mumbai: The rupee depreciated 20 paise to 92.40 against the US dollar in early trade on Thursday, as higher crude oil prices and the US administration's proposed tariff hikes against India fuelled dollar demand and weighed on the local unit.
Foreign fund inflows favoured the Indian currency, but it faced pressure after crude oil prices reversed easing, hovering above the USD 95-per-barrel level, according to forex traders.
They also said the Donald Trump administration's latest proposal to escalate the trade war with major trading partners raised inflation fears.

The US on Wednesday proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India, with a provision to cap them at 17 per cent if the two countries agree to a bilateral trade deal, giving it a slight edge over Asian competitors.
The proposed tariffs followed investigations by the US Trade Representative into 16 economic jurisdictions.
The USTR investigation report accused India of engaging in a range of acts, policies, and practices that create, maintain, or contribute to structural excess capacity and production.
India rejected the allegation and said the country is committed to working closely with the United States for an early conclusion of a bilateral trade agreement.
In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.50 and gained up to 92.39 before falling again to 92.40 against the greenback, trading 20 paise lower from its previous close.
On Wednesday, the rupee jumped 65 paise to settle at 92.20, the highest level this fiscal year so far.
The level was compared to the closing level of 92.28 against the greenback recorded on March 16 this year.
In the past seven weeks, the Indian currency has recovered nearly 5 per cent compared to its lowest-ever closing mark of 96.88 versus the US dollar seen on October 8.
Meanwhile, the dollar index, which gauges the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was at 103.79, higher by 0.17 per cent.

article_sentences: The Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy fixture between Rajasthan and Bengal got off to a delayed start at the Wankhede Stadium on Thursday after Rajasthan’s kit bags apparently arrived late at the venue.

With the toss scheduled for 10.30 am and the match set to begin at 11 am, it emerged that although the Rajasthan team had reached the stadium after travelling from its hotel near Terminal 2 of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, its kit bags were missing.
The kits eventually arrived around 11 am, following which the toss was conducted and the match began at 11.15 am, resulting in a 15-minute delay.
No overs were lost.
“The vehicle carrying the kits was stuck in heavy traffic, which led to the delay.
That’s why the match referee gave us some additional time.
Such things happen, and even in the past, during one of the games in Jaipur, the kits reached the venue late.
So, it’s nothing new,” a Rajasthan team source confirmed to Sportstar.
It remains to be seen what match referee Abhinav Bali records in his report about the delay.
This is the second consecutive time Bengal has been involved in a match that did not start as scheduled.
A couple of days ago, its fixture against Uttar Pradesh at the MCA-BKC ground was delayed because of slight dampness on the surface.
The umpires eventually reduced the contest to 15 overs per side, with Bengal going on to register a victory.
